sections.h2: Which offices handle property tax in McCracken County?
sections.html:
Three offices touch a McCracken County tax bill, and each has a separate job. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) sets the value, the Sheriff's Office collects the money, and the County Clerk takes over the paperwork once a bill goes delinquent. The PVA's own website states that it does not bill or collect, so walking into the assessment office with a check will get you redirected.

The PVA works from 621 Washington Street in Paducah, Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and answers at (270) 444-4712. Its staff values real and tangible property across the county. The few exceptions, such as public service companies, are valued by the state Revenue Cabinet in Frankfort. The Sheriff's tax page says in-person payments are taken weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. during the collection season, and county government as a whole is based at 300 Clarence Gaines Street.

sections.h2: When are McCracken County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills become payable to the Sheriff on November 1 and stay open until April 15 of the following year. The county's delinquent-tax FAQ says notices reach owners in late September or early October. The state schedule in KRS 134.015 then sets the price of waiting:

  • Paid in full on or before November 1: the bill less 2 percent. The 2026 discount date has already passed.
  • November 2 through December 31: the amount printed on the bill.
  • January: a 5 percent penalty.
  • February onward: a 10 percent penalty.
  • Close of business April 15: anything still unpaid moves from the Sheriff to the County Clerk.

Payment can be made at the counter, by mail, by phone, or online through a button that the Sheriff's site says is live from November through April. Card and e-check payments carry a convenience fee charged by the outside processor, and the amount is shown before you confirm. If a lender escrows your taxes, remember that the Sheriff mails the bill only to the owner of record, so call the lender before paying twice.

sections.h2: What does a McCracken County tax bill add up to?
sections.html:
The state's 2025 real property rate is 10.6 cents per $100 of assessed value, one notch below the 10.9 cents used for 2024. On a house at the Census median of $188,100, that state piece alone comes to about $199.39. City, school, library, fire and county rates go on top, and the PVA's page lists those taxing bodies as the ones that build on its assessments.

Since the 2024 bills, McCracken County has also added a 911 fee. The Sheriff's page says most properties see $46.26 more because of it, and the 2 percent early-pay discount does not apply to that line. Worth knowing before you estimate a closing credit.

sections.h2: How does a McCracken County owner dispute an assessment?
sections.html:
Start with a conference at the PVA office, because Kentucky does not allow a filed appeal without one. The tax roll then sits open to inspection for 13 days beginning the first Monday in May.

  • Hold the conference with the PVA or a deputy, who must explain how your number was reached and keep a written record of the meeting.
  • File the appeal with the County Clerk by the close of business on the day after inspection ends.
  • Bring evidence about the land and buildings: insurance papers, construction costs, and recent sale listings. The state says an appeal without such proof is denied.
  • Attend the local board of assessment appeals, which convenes 25 to 35 days after the inspection period closes.

A paid representative must belong to a category the Department of Revenue lists, such as an attorney, CPA or certified appraiser, and carries written authorization from you. If the board lands above the value you claimed after bills have gone out, a supplemental bill covers the difference. The Sheriff's page adds a separate warning: unreported additions or improvements that leave an assessment significantly understated can draw a 20 percent penalty.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the homestead exemption in McCracken County?
sections.html:
Owners who are 65 or older, or who are classed as totally disabled, can claim it. For the 2025 and 2026 assessment years the deduction is $49,100, taken off the assessed value before the rate is applied.

On a $188,100 home, the taxable amount drops to $139,000 and the state's share shrinks to roughly $147.34. Applications go to the McCracken County PVA, not the Sheriff. Proof of age can be a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. Disability claimants must show total disability under a federal or retirement-system program and generally reapply each year, unless they are veterans with a service-connected disability or were found totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems. The PVA's website adds that a formal application has to be on file before any exemption is granted.

sections.h2: What happens to unpaid McCracken County taxes when the house sells?
sections.html:
They follow the property. After April 15 an unpaid bill becomes a certificate of delinquency at the County Clerk, a lien is recorded, and interest of 1 percent per month starts. State law keeps that lien alive for 11 years under KRS 134.420 regardless of who owns the house, so a buyer's title search will find it.

The County Attorney's office handles collection under an agreement with the Department of Revenue. Its letters warn that continued non-payment can end in foreclosure, and a bill covered by a compliant payment plan is marked unavailable for sale to investors. The Clerk's annual sale of delinquent bills normally takes place in October. A buyer at that sale must notify the owner within 50 days, can add its own charges, and may sue to foreclose one year after the certificate was created. Settling the balance before April 15 avoids the clerk's and attorney's fees, so request a payoff figure from the Sheriff before you list.

sections.h2: What is it like to sell a house in McCracken County?
sections.html:
McCracken County covers 268 square miles in the far west of Kentucky, in the Jackson Purchase, with the Ohio River forming its northern edge and the Tennessee River its northeastern one. It was created in 1825 and is the central county of the Paducah, KY-IL metro area. Paducah is the county seat and the only incorporated city. Farley, Hendron, Massac and Reidland are census-designated places, and Lone Oak, Heath and West Paducah are among the unincorporated communities that appear on the map.

River and rail traffic built the local economy, and the Illinois Central once ran what was described as the largest operating and maintenance base in the world here. Public schooling comes from McCracken County Public Schools and Paducah Public Schools, and West Kentucky Community and Technical College is in Paducah. The county keeps Central time, and Census data put the mean commute at 17.6 minutes.

Roughly 69 percent of homes are owner-occupied and 170 building permits were issued in 2025, so most sales involve an existing house. When a property carries back taxes, deferred repairs or a lien, a cash purchase that closes as-is can settle the tax payoff and the sale together.

faqs.q: Does the McCracken County PVA collect property tax payments?
faqs.a: No. The PVA values property and handles exemptions, and the Sheriff's Office collects the tax. Take payments to the Sheriff, not to 621 Washington Street.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay McCracken County taxes to the Sheriff?
faqs.a: April 15, at close of business. After that the Sheriff cannot collect the prior-year bill, and it moves to the County Clerk with added interest and fees.

faqs.q: Is the 911 fee on McCracken County tax bills discounted?
faqs.a: No. The Sheriff's site says the 911 fee, added with the 2024 bills, is excluded from the 2 percent discount. Most properties pay $46.26 for it.

faqs.q: How big is the McCracken County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. Owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled, apply at the PVA office.

faqs.q: Can I sell a McCracken County house that has delinquent taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The balance is paid from the sale proceeds, or the buyer takes the property subject to the lien. Ask the Sheriff or County Clerk for the exact payoff before closing.
